chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of joking, for it removes the water (dignity) of the face.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah; a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمِزَاح: Joking, playful banter, or lighthearted speech
key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Water of the face; a metaphor for dignity, composure, or the lustre of countenance

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of joking on a person's dignity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against excessive joking (*al-mizah*), linking it to a loss of *ma' al-wajh* (the 'water of the face'), a metaphor for dignity, presence, and spiritual composure. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *haya'* (modesty/shyness) and *wajr* (dignity), suggesting that frivolity can erode the gravitas required for spiritual and social leadership. The advice is not a prohibition of all humor but a caution against its excess, which distracts from mindfulness (*muraqabah*) and self-respect.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the joking, for it removes with the water (dignity) of the face’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Beware of jokes; it takes away the dignity of one’s face.’”
